analysis.title: "The Crowding Out Effect Is Immense": Broadcom, Oracle Join SpaceX In AI Chip-Debt SPV Stampede
key_insights: Within about a week the AI ecosystem has lined up roughly $150B in chip-collateralized debt: SpaceX about $40B, Broadcom's Anthropic financing $60B (syndication started last week), and Broadcom's OpenAI chip financing of $50B+ (Bloomberg says possibly around $30B for the next leg). Oracle's deal is not yet sized and is not in the total.

Per the WSJ, Broadcom has spent weeks arranging more than $50B of financing for OpenAI's custom AI chip, approaching Apollo and Blackstone among lenders. It could include several gigawatts of OpenAI chip capacity and is expected to close before year-end. Bloomberg says no formal process has begun.
Broadcom's Anthropic deal: banks sent syndication letters last week for a $42B Class A senior-secured tranche. Blackstone leads an $18B Class B junior tranche and commits $9B of its own funds.

Oracle is in talks with Apollo and Goldman Sachs to fund a chip purchase through an off-balance-sheet vehicle. The WSJ says the aim is to bridge the gap between paying for hardware and receiving cloud revenue, and to keep debt costs under control. The likely structure is a separate company that buys the chips and leases them to Oracle. Size is undisclosed.

Oracle's 2056 bonds fell to a record low two weeks ago after the force majeure at Project Jupiter, yielding over 8%, wider than the average single-B junk bond. The Jupiter loans trade at 89-91 cents. Of the roughly $80B of project debt backing Oracle-leased data centers, three of four deals are short-dated bank loans against 15-19 year leases, which depend on refinancing in 2028-2032.

SpaceX seeks about $10B of bank loans plus $30B of IG debt to buy Nvidia chips, led by Apollo with Pimco circling. This follows a record $86B June IPO and $25B of bonds two weeks later, so $65B of debt since June, or 76% of IPO proceeds.

SpaceX 5Y CDS widened almost 15bp to a record, from about 181bp to 197bp. That exceeds the late-July high of about 188bp, is up about 30% since mid-September, and compares with about 110bp at the June IPO. SpaceX 2056 bonds trade around 85 cents.

Hyperscaler, data center and AI infrastructure IG and HY issuance is at least $360B this year per Bloomberg, or 5.8% of global bond sales versus 1.9% last year. Goldman's Adam Crook counts $575B+ of global gross AI-related debt issuance this year, with hyperscalers about 40%. Morgan Stanley expects a busier fall and 4Q as focus shifts to 2027 capex.

ZeroHedge's tracker shows hyperscaler off-balance-sheet liabilities of $3.8T at Sept 30, up $700B from June 30. With $250B of hyperscaler IG debt, the DV01 issued by the AI ecosystem in Q3 was about 25% higher than all Treasury issuance.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky calls the crowding-out effect potentially immense. His argument is that AI borrowers expecting 20-30% IRRs will borrow at high single-digit rates, which strains consumers, small businesses and governments, and may explain why real yields refuse to fall. He sees two outcomes: AI becomes self-financing via organic cash flow (making the next hyperscaler earnings important), or capital is rationed elsewhere and weaker parts of the economy break.

USD CCC spreads closed Wednesday at 998bp per Goldman credit sales strats, up 219bp in three months and 123bp in one month, in the 99th percentile of the past year. The IG index was unchanged at 80bp. Privorotsky says the Russell has underperformed the Nasdaq in 17 of the last 20 sessions.

Treasury yields: 10Y back up to 5.31% in Asia per Reuters, a day after a strong 10Y auction. The 30Y auction is today, with yields around 5.70%. JPMorgan's Brian Heavey said price action is bearish early, with the Recession basket leading and Beta and rate-sensitive names lagging, and that the SpaceX bond raise continues to pressure government bonds.

Apollo is involved in all three of this week's deals, Broadcom's June 20GW platform, xAI's Colossus financing and Nvidia's $500B compute financing platform from August, which concentrates exposure including Athene life insurance policies.

The deals are circular financing: the chip supplier (Broadcom) arranges money for buyers (OpenAI, Anthropic) who lack the balance sheets to buy hardware, similar to Nvidia with xAI. OpenAI and Broadcom announced a plan a year ago to co-develop 10GW of custom chips from 2H26 through 2029.

market_movers.rationale: Broadcom is arranging $60B for Anthropic and $50B+ for OpenAI chip purchases, financing its own customers. Broadcom bonds hit all-time lows after the Anthropic deal per ZeroHedge.
Oracle cannot borrow cheaply in its own name and is seeking an off-balance-sheet chip SPV. Its CDS is at records, 2056 bonds yield over 8%, and Jupiter loans trade at 89-91 cents.

sector_views.rationale: CCC spreads near 1,000bp while IG is unchanged at 80bp. Heavy AI borrowing is crowding out weaker borrowers.

earnings_insights: Privorotsky says the next hyperscaler earnings are particularly important to show whether AI can become self-financing from organic cash flow. No specific figures are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yield rose on the prospect of more corporate AI debt competing with sovereign issuance, a day after a strong 10Y auction.
The 30Y auction is today. Privorotsky argues a strong auction won't fix much as buyers are offered IG chip paper.
Up 219bp in three months and 123bp in one month, 99th percentile of the past year, signalling stress at the bottom of the capital structure.
Unchanged over three months, so the top of the capital structure is unaffected.

risk_factors: Crowding out of non-AI borrowers by AI debt issuance, which pushes up real yields and Treasury yields.
Chip collateral depreciates faster than buildings, so chip SPVs carry greater collateral risk.
Oracle refinancing risk in 2028-2032 on short-dated loans against 15-19 year leases.
Concentration of lenders, especially Apollo, across AI financings, with exposure through Athene life insurance.
Circular financing, with suppliers funding customers who lack balance sheets or income statements.
Rationing of capital to weaker parts of the economy if AI does not become self-financing.
vol_and_positioning: SpaceX 5Y CDS at a record 197bp, up about 30% since mid-September. Oracle CDS is at record highs. Paramount CDS is at financial-crisis levels per ZeroHedge's tweet.
Russell 2000 has underperformed the Nasdaq in 17 of the last 20 sessions per Privorotsky.
JPMorgan's Heavey: early price action bearish, Recession basket leading, Beta and rate-sensitive lagging.

tension_points.bull_case: If scarce compute generates 20-30% compounding IRRs, AI borrowers will borrow at high single-digit rates, and AI could become self-financing from organic cash flow.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital gets rationed elsewhere and weaker parts of the economy break. CCC spreads at 998bp and Russell underperformance are early signs, while real yields stay high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The next hyperscaler earnings showing AI generating enough organic cash flow to be increasingly self-financing.

theme_stances.key_argument: AI borrowing is raising real and sovereign yields and rationing capital for weaker borrowers.
theme_stances.evidence: The crowding out effect is potentially immense.
